purpose: Show operators and administrators how AI can support retrieval, documentation, handoffs, exception recognition, and service work while preserving the official record and qualified authority.
staffSummary: Build M45 around one consequential utility situation and one decision: Choose one task that may receive bounded support and define the source, review, record, and escalation path. The learner must leave with a usable operator-administrator AI support card, not a collection of definitions.
openingSituation: An operator needs the current procedure during a night shift while an administrator must ensure the resulting note enters the correct official record.
learnerDecision: Choose one task that may receive bounded support and define the source, review, record, and escalation path.
analogy: A good relief worker makes the next shift stronger by leaving a clear handoff. AI support should improve the handoff without becoming the operator.
learnerOutcomes: Explain The Operator and Administrator in plain English and connect it to a real water, wastewater, stormwater, or One Water decision.
Distinguish operating observation, advisory support, official record, draft, approval, shift handoff, and qualified authority without using one term to hide several different jobs.
Analyze the module situation, identify missing evidence, and name the professional consequence of a weak decision.
Compare how the same question changes across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, administration, engineering, finance, technology, and public leadership.

Evaluate sources, assumptions, limitations, permissions, and human authority using this boundary: Do not position AI as an operator, certified decision-maker, records officer, or replacement for local procedures and qualifications.
Create a usable operator-administrator AI support card with evidence, roles, limits, review steps, and the next accountable action.
Defend the recommendation to Foundation, Practitioner, and Leader audiences while keeping disagreement and uncertainty visible.
curriculumOutcomes: Give The Operator and Administrator one clear learning job inside Role-Based Practice.
Connect the module to a consequential decision and the operator-administrator AI support card.
Preserve current content, proposals, enhancements, and contributor records by stable identifier.
Separate verified evidence, Hardeep positions, expert interpretation, instructional scenarios, and unresolved questions.
Create an explicit bridge to the preceding and following modules without duplicating their work.
marketingOutcomes: Describe the practical value as helping a learner make and explain this decision: Choose one task that may receive bounded support and define the source, review, record, and escalation path.
Name the operator-administrator AI support card as the visible result of the module.
Do not promise savings, compliance, certification, safety, performance, implementation success, or career outcomes without separately approved evidence.
definitionOfDone: The learner explains the core distinctions, completes the required evidence and decision activities, passes distributed checks, saves a complete operator-administrator AI support card, and names the next accountable action.
scopeBoundary: Do not position AI as an operator, certified decision-maker, records officer, or replacement for local procedures and qualifications.
researchQuestions: What must an intelligent newcomer understand about The Operator and Administrator before using it in utility work?
Which sources can support the distinctions among operating observation, advisory support, official record, draft, approval, shift handoff, and qualified authority?
What evidence would allow a practitioner to make this decision: Choose one task that may receive bounded support and define the source, review, record, and escalation path.
Which failure modes, counterexamples, and edge conditions could make the operator-administrator AI support card misleading?
How does the question change across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, reuse, finance, engineering, administration, technology, and public accountability?
Which actions require qualified operator, engineer, water-quality, cybersecurity, privacy, legal, procurement, records, finance, accessibility, or executive review?
Which claims remain outside the module boundary: Do not position AI as an operator, certified decision-maker, records officer, or replacement for local procedures and qualifications.
